title: rowshape.com SEO backlog
surface: docs-site/ (Astro 7 + Starlight 0.41, deployed to Cloudflare Pages at https://rowshape.com)
how_this_works: One iteration fixes one SEO element end to end: change, build, `npm run check`, commit. Work that cannot finish in one iteration stays here as an open story and is picked up next iteration. Every story records what was VERIFIED, not what was intended.

audit_baseline.method: built docs-site locally (49 pages) and read the emitted dist/
already_good: sitemap-index.xml + sitemap-0.xml emitted by Astro 7 automatically; 49 URLs, all absolute against site: https://rowshape.com
meta description present in frontmatter on all 48 content pages - zero missing
og:title, og:type, og:url, og:locale, og:description, og:site_name emitted
internal link checker + 32KB client-JS budget already enforced in scripts/check-build.mjs
no framework runtime shipped; fast by construction
gaps_found: NO robots.txt at all - crawlers get a 404 and the sitemap is undiscoverable except via the <link rel=sitemap> hint
NO og:image / twitter:image on any page, while twitter:card is declared summary_large_image - every share renders as a blank card
homepage <title> is 'rowshape | rowshape' - the site title is appended to a page title that already is the site title
no JSON-LD anywhere: no SoftwareApplication, no BreadcrumbList, no TechArticle
/pagefind/ search-index fragments are crawlable JSON with no canonical
27 findings pages carry generic RS-CODE titles rather than the problem language a developer would search
no llms.txt / AI-crawler surface, on a product whose whole wedge is the agent loop
check-build.mjs guards links and JS weight but asserts nothing about head metadata

stories.title: robots.txt, generated from astro.config's site so it cannot drift
verified: dist/robots.txt is emitted by the build and names https://rowshape.com/sitemap-index.xml, which exists in dist/
/pagefind/ is disallowed; /_astro/ deliberately is not

scripts/check-build.mjs now fails the build if robots.txt is missing, names no sitemap, names one that is not in dist/, or starts blocking render assets — negative-tested by hand-editing dist/robots.txt and watching both assertions fire

stories.title: og:image + twitter:image - a real social card, and the head tags that point at it
verified: public/og.png (1200x630, 55 KiB) generated by `npm run og` and committed; rendered and eyeballed, not assumed
og:image, og:image:type/width/height/alt and twitter:image emitted on all 49 pages, absolute against the new SITE constant
check-build.mjs reads the PNG IHDR and fails if any page lacks og:image, declares a relative one, omits twitter:image, points at a file not in dist/, or advertises dimensions the file does not have
negative test found a real defect in the first version of the guard: it deduped by image URL, so one bad page was masked by the other 48. Fixed to key on the whole triple and re-tested.
stories.notes: The card is committed rather than built in CI on purpose: rasterizing SVG text goes through the host fontconfig, so a CI runner without the font renders the text as nothing and no downstream check would see it.

stories.title: Title template: kill 'rowshape | rowshape', keep titles under 60 chars
verified: homepage <title> was "rowshape | rowshape"; it is now "rowshape — the type-checker for database migrations" (50 chars)
frontmatter seoTitle added to the docs schema (max 60, optional) and applied to all 27 findings pages, which ran 51-110 chars
longest <title> on the site is now 56 chars; every one of the 49 is unique
src/starlightRouteData.ts is a Starlight route middleware; where seoTitle is absent behaviour is unchanged, and og:title is deliberately left as the full sentence
check-build.mjs fails on a missing title, one over 60 chars, one that repeats itself across the delimiter, or two pages sharing one — negative-tested on all three

stories.title: Meta descriptions in the length a result renders, plus the head-metadata guard
stories.note: Land early - it guards every later story.
verified: audited first: canonical present on all 49 pages and exactly one h1 per page — both already correct, so nothing was invented to fix
20 descriptions rewritten into the 70-160 range; they ran 25 to 349 chars, and RS-PERF-010 opened by naming RS-PERF-002, which is a fine sentence in context and a useless snippet in a result
every rewrite is a compression of that page's own description or opening paragraph — no page makes a claim it did not already make
the guard found a real duplicate on its first run: dist/404.html carried the site-wide description, identical to the homepage. The 404 now has its own content and description.
check-build.mjs fails on a missing description, one over 160, one under 70, or two pages sharing one — negative-tested on the floor and the ceiling

stories.title: JSON-LD SoftwareApplication on the homepage
verified: homepage emits a schema.org @graph of Organization + WebSite + SoftwareApplication; parsed back out of dist/index.html, not assumed
every claim is checkable in the repo: MIT from LICENSE, "macOS, Linux, Windows" from .goreleaser.yaml goos, Go from go.mod, the install and reference URLs from the pages that exist
no aggregateRating, and the guard REFUSES one — inventing ratings is how a site gets its structured data distrusted wholesale

the client-JS budget no longer charges JSON-LD: it is a data block the browser never executes, and making metadata compete with a budget meant to keep framework runtimes out would get the metadata dropped

SITE and REPO moved into src/site.ts, imported by both astro.config.mjs and the route middleware — iteration 2 had left a second copy of the origin, which is exactly the drift robots.txt was written to avoid
guard negative-tested on a fabricated aggregateRating and on malformed JSON

stories.title: JSON-LD BreadcrumbList + TechArticle on docs pages
verified: all 47 docs pages emit BreadcrumbList + TechArticle; homepage keeps SoftwareApplication; the 404 carries none, matching its exclusion from the sitemap
trails read rowshape > Findings > RS-LOCK-001, and a section index page is its section rather than its own child
a new top-level section with no label in SECTIONS FAILS THE BUILD rather than emitting a raw slug — negative-tested by adding a /faq/ page and watching the build refuse it
check-build.mjs also verifies breadcrumb positions are 1..n and that the trail ends at the page it is on — negative-tested by rewriting a position

TechArticle deliberately carries no datePublished/dateModified: both need the git commit date of the source, which the middleware cannot reach. SEO-11 adds them. An absent date is valid, an invented one is not.

stories.title: Findings pages: search-intent descriptions and on-page copy across all 27 codes
stories.note: Titles were handled in iteration 3 via the seoTitle mechanism. What remains here is the meta descriptions and the on-page problem language.

stories.title: Internal linking: related findings, and findings <-> CLI reference cross-links
verified: measured the link graph first, and the first measurement was WRONG — it read the whole page instead of <main> and reported 47 orphans. Re-measured against <main>: only / and /404 lack in-content inbound links, both correctly.

the real gap was that the link checker SKIPPED relative links as "rare in Starlight output", while the finding catalog links all 27 of its pages as ./rs-lock-001/ — the densest set of internal links on the site was the one set nothing verified

unskipping them found two live 404s: /agent/mcp/ linked ./rule/ (resolves to /agent/mcp/rule/, which does not exist) and the GitHub Action page linked ../internal/verdict/verdict.go, a repo path that is not a docs route. Both fixed at source; docs/action.md regenerated and tools/gencli tests pass.
a remark plugin now links every mention of a finding code to its page: 5 real cross-references that were plain text are now links, and every future mention is linked without anyone remembering to
the plugin skips codes with no page, self-references, fenced code blocks, and anything already inside a link
check-build.mjs now fails if the catalog does not link a finding page, or if any page links to itself — negative-tested

stories.title: Homepage H1 and above-the-fold copy carry the query language, not only the metaphor
llms.txt + AI-crawler surface
verified: /llms.txt generated from the content collection (not hand-written), listing all 47 content pages with their descriptions under ordered sections
a page not claimed by a section falls into a catch-all rather than being dropped silently
robots.txt points at it in a comment — there is no standard directive, and a comment costs nothing
check-build.mjs fails if llms.txt and the sitemap disagree in either direction — negative-tested on both

this is not claimed as a ranking signal. It matters because rowshape's wedge is being the tool inside an agent's turn, and an agent inferring the CLI surface from rendered HTML full of nav chrome is the failure it removes.

stories.title: Sitemap <lastmod> and article dateModified, both from git
stories.note: Also supplies dateModified for the TechArticle nodes added in iteration 6 — same git-date map, two consumers.
verified: the sitemap was 49 bare <loc> elements; every URL now carries a <lastmod> that is the git commit date of that page source
the same map feeds dateModified on every TechArticle, so a page cannot advertise two different freshness dates — check-build.mjs compares them as instants and fails if they disagree
gen-lastmod.mjs REFUSES a shallow clone rather than degrading, and that guard fired for real: this session's own checkout was shallow, which would have given all 49 pages one identical date
docs-deploy.yml now checks out with fetch-depth: 0 in both jobs — actions/checkout defaults to 1, so CI was exactly the case the guard describes
no datePublished: it would be the file's first commit, a date about the file rather than the content
a page not yet committed simply gets no date, in the sitemap and in the article

@astrojs/sitemap declared as a direct dependency (Starlight adds its own only when absent, so this replaces rather than duplicates); package-lock.json edited surgically, one line, and npm ci verified from a clean node_modules
guard negative-tested on a future date and on a missing lastmod

stories.title: 404 page: useful, indexable-as-noindex, and links back into the tree
stories.note: Partly done in iteration 4: the 404 now has its own title, description and links into the tree. What remains is the noindex header and confirming Cloudflare Pages serves it with a 404 status rather than a 200.

stories.title: Core Web Vitals: font loading, CLS on the hero, preconnect audit
Heading hierarchy and semantic structure audit across all 49 pages
Rollup: re-run the full audit against the built site and close or re-open every story
Reference-page descriptions come from cobra `Short` lines and are 25-69 chars
stories.detail: The ten /reference/ pages are generated by `go run ./tools/gencli` from the command tree, and their description IS the command's Short help line — pinned by a staleness test in tools/gencli/gen_test.go. Lengthening them means editing CLI help text, where terse is correct. The options are: (a) leave them and accept a synthesized snippet, (b) give gencli a separate longer docs blurb per command, (c) lengthen the Short lines. This is why check-build.mjs exempts /reference/ from the description FLOOR and not from the ceiling.
